chapter: Lester Young and the early Basie years
title: The ride from Newport and Prez's money troubles
summary: Prez rides with Tate, says Jo Jones lent him money and reviews the books.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: things would always come to Sherman, you know, and all the bands would come there to play and I'd catch all of them. But anyway, I was with him -- he asked me, says, "How are you going home?" It was hard to get back to New York, Gary. You had to go to Providence and wait a long time and take a bus to Providence and wait and maybe miss a train, then catch a train from Providence to New York. So he was up there, he and his lady, he had his lady and a friend that had driven him there and a Cadillac. He's sitting in the back in the middle of the seat like the way those big engines ride down in Oklahoma, you know, big hat on. So he says, "You ride with me." I said, "Well, I'd love to, Prez." He says, "You've got to. You don't go back over there. You ride with me." So I says, "Okay." He says, "And as a matter of fact, I want you to be my manager today, to take care of my business for me, pick up my money." He was playing at the Birdland. He says, "They docked me, you know. They're not going to pay me for the night." He said, "But that's all right." He says, -- I went on, he heard me play a set. So he said, "Gee, you sound good. I've been back here listening. You've got it together. You really sound good." He says, "I haven't done too well, you know." He says, "I've been down right to rock bottom." He says, "I started to call on you because I've been reading about you. I started to call on you." I used to let him have money, you know, a lot of times. He used to like to gamble,

you know, and lose his money and I'd loan him money, a hundred or something like that because I didn't have any of those habits, see. So he says -- I said, "Well, what the hell. You know if I got anything, you're part of it. Why didn't you?" I says, "You know that." He says, "I know that, but a man's got his pride. You know, a man must have his pride." He says, "I've been down to -- I've called on some others --" I won't call any names "-- that turned me down. I didn't only want like 50 or 75 dollars." He says, "You know who came to my rescue?" Says, "Miss Jones, Lady Jo Jones." Jo Jones was working with Joe Bushkin then. He was very busy, working all over New York, making good money. Jo Jones went down to the Alvin Hotel and signed his name, he said, "Let him fill it in." He says, "Whatever you fill in, it's all right." He just signed his name and put a check there, says, "Let him fill it in."

And he says, "That's who came to my rescue." And I says, "Well, I really didn't know that." And he had left home, he said he couldn't get along, he said, "I can't think no more, I can't practice because I can't get along at home." So he had moved to the Alvin Hotel.
So, you know, I tell you, when I got in the car that night with him, first thing he did, he opened his wallet like this and turned me on, you know. He lit up. He said, "Now, let's review the books."
